correctness.rationale: For a given periodic set of size k, its permutation contributes k!, and the complete-graph rooted forest determinant for the other vertices is k*n^(n-k-1) (one forest when k=n). This gives k*(n)_k/n^(k+1) and the telescoping tail (n)_k/n^k. Exchangeability gives independent uniform cyclic sets conditional on their sizes. The logarithm of the tail at k asymptotic to x*sqrt(n) tends to -x^2/2; the Gaussian tail bound ensures all fixed rescaled moments are uniformly integrable. For the fixed-size conditional array, selecting all distinct witnesses gives exactly (n)_L times the product of (m_i)_(d_i)/(n)_(d_i), with the claimed Poisson factorial limit. Any cross-pair collision forces one witness to demand at least three distinct memberships, giving a loss of at least n^(-1/2); there are only finitely many witness partitions for each fixed moment. A single intersection has factorial moments bounded by (m_i*m_j/n)^a, hence Hölder gives a joint exponential-moment bound when the sizes are O(sqrt(n)). This justifies Poisson moment convergence. Conditional convergence along every deterministic sequence with positive size limits and weak convergence of the size vector (or a Skorokhod coupling of the sizes) gives the claimed Rayleigh mixing for fixed q. For the empty probability, the Rayleigh double integral factors using r+s and r/(r+s), giving 1/3. Independently, summing the exact probability of disjoint sets of sizes a,b gives a*b*(n)_(a+b)/n^(a+b+2); collecting terms by a+b yields (E[K^2]-1)/(6*n), confirming 1/3 by moment convergence. Given the shared map's cyclic set, adjacent overlaps are independent with common conditional expectation K_i*E[K]/n, giving the asserted covariance, while disjoint pairs use independent maps. The mean and variance of the one-pair mixed Poisson follow from E[R]=sqrt(pi/2) and E[R^2]=2.
residual_risks: The proof fixes q and does not estimate a rate; single-pair rational checks are not a finite-q array proof. Periodic set intersections are not common directed cycles or edges.

evidence: Nualart–Zhang Theorem 3.8 bounds a multivariate hypergeometric approximation for counts of distinct fixed colors in one sample; its general Theorem 2.6 bounds independent-Poisson approximation through size-biased coupling errors.

Rybarczyk–Stark use independent Bernoulli features and count unweighted induced subgraphs of an intersection graph whose vertex count grows. Resultary 278e7537a80c handles overlaps of exchangeable matchings and has a nonmixed Poisson limit in its circle model.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The urn model includes the one-edge conditional law and can aid successive-set comparisons after removing multiply occupied labels. It is not itself the vector of all edge counts for multiple independent fixed-size subsets. The general size-bias bound can handle that conditional vector via an additional two-set inclusion coupling and vanishing cross-pair errors. Neither application yields random Rayleigh means or the joint law across mappings without the model-specific analysis. The intersection graph result discards edge multiplicities and has different scaling.

evidence: Conditional on two sizes the pair overlap is hypergeometric, so its fixed-mean Poisson approximation is not original. The published coupling bound could be used conditionally for all pairs by forcing a uniformly chosen witness into both relevant sets; cross-pair changes must be bounded to make that argument work.

Cyclic counts fluctuate at order sqrt(n), leaving random rates and nonzero shared-map covariance. The matching analogue instead gives independent Poisson(2/9) overlaps decoupled from its Gaussian size fluctuations.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The independent-Poisson approximation is an ingredient and replaceable by known methods. The audited overlap law still has to establish joint conditional asymptotics for the cyclic-set model and retain the nondegenerate size mixing, then evaluate the mixed empty probability. In particular, plugging a mean size into a known Poisson approximation would produce the wrong independence and empty probability. No inspected stronger theorem directly gives the combined mapping claim.

originality.rationale: The one-map cyclic law and general Poisson approximation are classical, and the single deterministic pair is a hypergeometric special case. The checked sources do not give the random-mapping joint overlap array, its shared-map Rayleigh mixing and its exact empty probability. Strong approximation techniques can replace the proof of conditional Poisson asymptotics, with a model-specific comparison; neither the one-map distribution nor a Poisson approximation with deterministic means alone supplies the mapping array and its dependence.
residual_risks: Hansen–Jaworski's 2010 Random Mappings with a Given Number of Cyclical Points was not readable in the attempted OA retrieval; no noncoverage inference is drawn from that. A search hit about sqrt(n)-scale cyclic states in random automata failed lawful retrieval and was not used as exclusion evidence.
Earlier equivalent overlap results under random feature or urn terminology remain possible. The same-day date of analogous records is not used as a priority determination.

value.rationale: The overlap is a natural recurrence observable for independently chosen dynamics on the same labels. Each periodic set has vanishing relative size, yet common periodic vertices have limiting probability 2/3. The array resolves information lost by a one-pair Poisson heuristic: triple label coincidences vanish while overlaps sharing a map remain positively dependent because of its fluctuating cyclic-set size. This distinction and exact existence constant give useful benchmarks, not just a first-moment calculation.
residual_risks: No claim about common trajectories, growing numbers of maps or optimal approximation rates.
